planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in gritty, well-drained, humus-rich soil in filtered light rather than deep shade; this nearly chlorophyll-free miniature is slow and fragile, so avoid overwatering or heavy shade that invites rot.

directions: Solar Mouse is a diminutive, nearly pure-white sport in the Mouse Ears line of miniature hostas discovered by Bob Solberg at Green Hill Farm, grown by collectors mainly for the novelty of its stark ivory leaves. Because tissue with almost no chlorophyll cannot photosynthesize well, the plant stays notoriously weak and slow even under ideal care, and clumps are prone to stalling out or rotting if kept too wet or too shaded. Its fragility has made it more valuable as a breeding parent than as a garden plant, having passed its bright white margins on to the far more vigorous sport Mouse Madness. Give it bright, filtered light rather than dense shade and gritty, fast-draining soil to offset its weak constitution.
